_comment: Hand-reviewed corrections to the heuristic in scripts/tag_grammar.py. Keys are JLAB card 'order' values. 'untag' = heuristic fired on a vocabulary/usage remark; 'tag' = genuine new grammar point the heuristic missed.

tag.23: "janakatta" is the negative, past form of "da".
tag.89: Past tense for i-adjectives: Replace the last -i with -katta.
tag.93: Negative past tense for i-adjectives: Replace the last -i with -kunakatta.
tag.225: Relative verb clauses: a verb/sentence placed before a noun describes that noun (nomu hito = a person who drinks).
tag.230: Sentences ending on plain "da" cannot be used as a relative clause; inflections of da (janai, datta...) can.
tag.287: Particle combination "to no": combines the meanings of to (with) and no (possessive).
tag.299: In casual speech particles (ha, wo, ga...) are often omitted.
tag.371: The past polite/teineigo form is built with -mashita instead of -masu.
tag.624: hazu: should (be) / is supposed to, described by a relative clause.
tag.654: zenzen + negative sentence expresses "not at all / never".
tag.873: The -tari form also works for the state of being: da -> datta -> dattari.
tag.1772: nikui attached to the verb stem expresses that an action is difficult to do.
tag.2035: -te kudasaru: same meaning as -te kureru, one level more polite.
